caption: Hot water is poured from a kettle over a large block of ice on the ground, and the ice melts where the water hits it.

sa.check: A large block of ice sits on the ground.
Hot, steaming water is poured onto the block from a kettle.
The ice melts visibly where the water lands: wet, hollowed, running.
The kettle is visible as the source of the water.
The pour comes first and the melting follows it.

pc.expect: Where the hot water lands the ice turns glossy, hollows and shrinks; the change is cumulative and grows only while water keeps coming.
pc.fail: The hollow fills back in or the surface refreezes matt; or the block grows; or the melt spot moves to where no water fell.

pc.expect: The stream leaves a visible effect: wetting, a pit, run-off and possibly steam; the ice under the stream does not stay dry and sharp.
pc.fail: Water runs over the ice and it stays dry, frosted and unchanged; or the block melts evenly everywhere at once including where no water touched.

pc.expect: The poured water and the meltwater run down the block and pool on the ground.
pc.fail: Water climbs the block or flows uphill; or pools on top of the block's sloping face; or steam sinks and hugs the ground.

pc.expect: Ice stays a hard solid where the water has not reached; it may crack sharply from the heat but does not bend, sag or flow.
pc.fail: The block sags or bends like wax; or ice flows as a viscous lump; or the ice turns into snow or slush all over at once.

pc.expect: One block, one kettle; the block only loses matter and water comes only from the kettle.
pc.fail: The block vanishes at a stroke or a second block appears; or water appears on the ice with no stream; or the kettle vanishes; or the stream passes through the block.

pc.expect: The ground, the kettle and the ice's colour stay consistent.
pc.fail: The kettle changes colour or shape; or the ice turns coloured; or the ground changes texture away from the water.
